newsitem.title: USA: Tel Offshore natgas revenues jump.
newsitem.headline: Tel Offshore natgas revenues jump.

text.p: Tel Offshore Trust said the working interest owners of the trust's properties reported 122 percent quarter to quarter increase in natual gas revenues and a 10 percent decline in oil revenues.

The trust said natural gas revenues attributable to its third quarter distribution next month rose to $5,375,933 from $2,417,520 in the second quarter, due primarily to a 142 percent jump in volumes to 2.16 billion cubic feet.
The volume increase was due primarily to successful drilling of the B-5, B-8 and B-9 wells on the West Cameron 643 property in the second quarter, the trust noted.
It said the increase in natural gas volumes was slightly offset by a decrease in the average price received for natural gas to $2.48 per thousand cubic feet from $2.70 in the second quarter.

Crude oil revenues slipped to $2,644,626 from $2,922,715 in the previous quarter on an 8 percent decrease in volumes to 145,021 barrels, due primarily to the shut down of a booster pumping station, which caused high line pressure on the Eugene Island 339 property.
In addition, there was a decrease in the average price received for crude oil and condensate to $18.24 per barrel in the latest quarter from $18.49 per barrel in the prior quarter.
The trust said its share of capital expenditures increased by about $68,300 in the latest quarter due to drilling and completing the B-11, B-12 and F-2 wells on the Ship Shoal 182/183 property.
The quarterly deposit to the trust's Special Cost Escrow Account dropped to about $172,000 in the latest quarter from $316,000 in the previous quarter.
